title: Prefill-aware runtime hint cache + staged microprobe tuner
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Background: Kernel choice for attention and other compute primitives currently relies on coarse-grained offline profiling and static heuristics. That leads to suboptimal latency/cost under mixed workloads with variable sequence-length distributions and on heterogeneous GPU fleets.

Proposal: Implement a two-part runtime system: (1) a lightweight per-session Prefill Hint Cache that stores kernel-choice suggestions keyed by (model-family, arch-fingerprint, seqlen-bucket, token-phase) with associated confidence and TTL, and (2) a Staged Microprobe Tuner that opportunistically runs microbenchmarks on idle or warm GPUs to continuously refresh kernel latency estimates for hot (model/arch/seqlen) tuples. Together these components form a feedback loop that adapts kernel selection to live hardware characteristics and workload patterns without expensive full-model rebenchmarks.

Key ideas and differentiators: 
- Sequence-phase awareness: store separate hints for prefill vs decode and for token-phase bands (early, mid, long-tail) to avoid prefilling-decoding mismatches.
- Confidence-weighted caching: hints carry confidence scores derived from microprobe recency, variance, and observed request latency residuals. Router uses confidence to decide hedging, probe-triggering, or fallback.
- Staged microprobe budget: probes run in stages (sanity probe, microkernel latency sweep, end-to-end short-run) with configurable budget per node and global rate limits to avoid interference.
- Speculative hedging & safety fallback: when confidence low or telemetry shows tail risk, runtime can run short hedged decode on alternative kernel with rollback/fallback if output becomes unavailable or latency exceeds SLO.
- Telemetry fusion: correlate microprobe results with real request telemetry (p50/p95, cache hit fraction, GPU occupancy) to detect drift and invalidate hints automatically.
- Minimal surface area: defaults opt-in per customer; admin controls in Console to tune probe budgets and TTLs for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data model and cache API: design Hint struct (model_tag, arch_hash, seqlen_bucket, token_phase, kernel_id, confidence, ttl, last_probe_ts). Expose ephemeral in-memory cache with optional persistence to local SSD for Private/Dedicated.
2) Probe harness: small Rust/C++ microbench runner to measure kernel latency across a small set of op-variants. Controlled by a lightweight scheduler and capped by resource quotas.
3) Runtime integration: kernel selector consults Hint Cache first, falls back to cost-model if missing, and optionally triggers quick probe or hedged execution depending on policy.
4) Telemetry pipeline: new telemetry tags (hint_hit, hint_confidence, probe_id, probe_latency, probe_variance) emitted to Statsd/Grafana and batch sink for offline analysis.
5) Safety and rollout: implement canary rollout with per-customer opt-in, A/B switch in Console; automatic safe-revert on SLA regressions flagged by monitoring.

Benchmarks and success metrics:
- Primary success: 8-15% median latency improvement on mixed seqlen conversational workloads for canary customers, with no >=1% increase in error rate or p99 latency regressions.
- Secondary: 10-25% reduction in token-cost for latency-sensitive small models due to better kernel packing and reduced hedging.
- Operational: <0.5% probe-induced CPU/GPU interference (measured as excess load), and probe budget adherence.

Observability and dashboards:
- New Grafana panels: Hint Cache hit-rate by model/arch, probe success/latency histogram, hint confidence distribution, probe budget consumption, rollout impact.
- Alerting: spike in hint_miss_rate or p95 latency correlated with hint changes triggers rollback workflow.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (experiment): local dev + bench only. Implement cache and probe harness behind feature flag.
- Phase 1 (internal): enable on staging and run microprobe sweeps against test fleets. Validate metrics and low interference.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of hosted traffic (non-critical customers) with telemetry gating and automatic rollback.
- Phase 3 (gradual): expand to Dedicated/Private with admin controls, documentation, and SDK hooks.

Open design decisions:
- Seqlen bucketing granularity: fixed buckets (e.g., <32,32-128,128-512,>512) vs adaptive bucketing based on per-model histograms.
- Probe fidelity vs budget: number of runs and kernels to test per probe event.
- Persistence layer: ephemeral memory-only vs SSD-backed hint store for quick warm restarts.

Risks and mitigations:
- Probe interference: keep probes low-priority and run when GPU active fraction < threshold; monitor and abort if interference detected.
- Incorrect hint leading to SLA regression: use confidence score + hedging and only promote hints to high confidence after cross-checked microprobe and real-traffic observations.
- Privacy/compliance: for Private customers, probes must run within customer's VPC/cluster; no telemetry exported without consent.

acceptance_criteria: Hint Cache implemented with stable in-memory API and unit tests
Microprobe harness that can run non-intrusive kernel latency sweeps with configurable budget
Kernel selector consults hint cache and honors confidence/ttl semantics
Telemetry emitted for hint_hit, hint_confidence, probe_latency and visible in staging Grafana
Canary rollout executed for 5% of traffic with automatic rollback on SLA regressions
Documentation for Console controls and operator runbook completed
